title: Aura
tagline: An identity with the volume turned all the way up.
imageAlt: Aura brand identity — the red arch mark embossed on black stationery
lede: Designing a brand people feel before they hear it.
overview: Smart speakers won the countertop and lost the heart. Aura's identity started from a different question: what should sound look like? One red arch became the whole system — the mark, the packaging, the light ring on the product, and the accent that carries the launch site. Everything else stays near-black so the arch can do the talking.
problem: Speaker landing pages had become spec sheets — watts, drivers, and a grid of grey renders. Nothing about the category said atmosphere, and the delight was buried below the fold.
solution: One bold move: darkness. A near-black canvas lets the mark glow, the red arch does all the pointing, and the same gesture repeats from business card to boot screen. The identity shipped alongside the launch site and outperformed the old brand on every recall test we ran.

title: Ledger
imageAlt: Ledger brand identity — the L monogram debossed on a matte black card
lede: Making a custody brand feel as solid as a vault door.
overview: Custody platforms ask ordinary people to behave like security engineers. Ledger's brief was to move the confidence from the manual into the brand. We cut an L monogram with the profile of a stacked ledger, debossed it into matte black across every touchpoint, and carried the same plain-language voice into the product — balances, approvals, and signing all speak human first.
problem: Every existing flow treated the seed phrase ceremony as a test the user could fail. One mistyped word and people abandoned the product — or worse, photographed the phrase.
solution: A guided recovery ritual with clear checkpoints: the app confirms each step in plain words, approvals queue where you can see them, and the riskiest actions read differently from the safe ones. Support tickets about recovery dropped to near zero in beta.

title: Stride
tagline: A running coach that respects the run.
imageAlt: Stride brand identity — the S mark on white stationery with a green edge
lede: Stripping a fitness tracker back to the three numbers runners feel.
overview: Stride's founders came with a paradox: their app collected forty metrics and their users looked at three. We rebuilt the dashboard around pace, effort, and streak — everything else moved behind one deliberate tap. A single green ring became the whole status language: solid when you are on plan, breathing when it is rest day.
problem: The old dashboard was a cockpit. Runners mid-workout could not parse it at arm's length, and the post-run summary buried the one question that matters — was that better than last time?
solution: A glanceable mid-run screen with type sized for motion, a post-run story that leads with the comparison, and notifications that never interrupt a run in progress. Weekly retention rose 22% in the redesign cohort.

title: Verse
tagline: A writing partner that knows when to stay quiet.
imageAlt: Verse brand identity — the gold star mark foil-stamped on cream paper
lede: Interface patterns for AI that assists without taking the pen.
overview: Verse is a drafting tool for people who like writing. The founding constraint: the model may never type into the document. We designed a margin where suggestions wait — quiet, collapsed, dismissible with one key — and a review mode that shows the writer exactly what changed and why. The knot became our metaphor: ideas intertwined, never tangled.
problem: Early testers described AI writing tools as a co-author who grabs the keyboard. Acceptance rates looked healthy while trust cratered — people shipped text they could not defend.
solution: Suggestions live beside the text, not inside it. Each one carries its reasoning in a single sentence, and accepting is an edit the writer performs. Trust scores doubled, and the accept rate barely moved — which was exactly the point.
